title: Haya Peanut Sauce
localName: Ekitooke — Supu ya Karanga ya Wahaya
community: Haya people of Kagera — the Great Lakes peanut sauce tradition
author: Mama Salima
desc: Haya Ekitooke — the distinctive Haya peanut sauce of Kagera, made from freshly roasted and pounded groundnuts cooked with tomatoes, onions, and smoked fish into a thick, rich sauce. Served over matoke or ugali — the sauce that defines the Kagera kitchen.
longDesc: The Haya peanut sauce (ekitooke) is the defining condiment of Kagera cooking — richer and more complex than plain groundnut sauce because of the smoked fish addition, which adds a deep umami note that carries throughout the meal.
ingredients: 1 cup raw groundnuts — roasted and pounded coarsely
steps: Roast groundnuts until golden. Pound coarsely in mortar.
Heat oil. Cook onions until golden. Add tomatoes. Cook 6 minutes.
Add smoked fish. Stir to combine.
Mix pounded groundnuts with ½ cup warm water.
Add to the pot. Add remaining water.
chefTips: The smoked fish is what makes this Haya rather than generic peanut sauce.
Pound, do not blend — coarser texture is traditional.
commonMistakes: Using commercial peanut butter — entirely different character.
cookingScience: The smoked fish adds inosinate (IMP) — a nucleotide that acts synergistically with glutamate (from tomatoes) and guanylate (from peanuts) to produce umami intensity far greater than any single source alone. This is the umami synergy principle — the combination produces more than the sum of the parts.
sustainabilityTips: Smoked fish from Lake Victoria — preserved and transported sustainably.
healthBenefits: High protein from peanuts and fish.
culturalNote: Haya ekitooke is the taste that Kagera-born Tanzanians miss most when they leave their region — the particular combination of roasted groundnut, smoked fish, and tomato that defines home for the people of the Great Lakes.
